analysis: Market context: US equities are in a mixed/recovery phase after the April 2025 tariff-shock drawdown. Most candidates are basing in the lower half of their 52-week ranges — classic Stage 1-to-2 transition territory. Portfolio is near-full cash ($100K), giving clean optionality to deploy into 3 high-conviction setups without forcing anything. Three names stand out for combining compelling fundamental value with early technical confirmation of base formation: PYPL (cheapest large-cap fintech in years, confirmed uptrend basing), FTNT (cybersecurity secular compounder, confirmed uptrend and above SMA200), and ADBE (world-class creative/document software at historically cheap forward valuation near 52w lows). NNDM position is tiny (~$2) and irrelevant to sizing. Total proposed equity deployment ~67%, keeping ~$33K cash as a buffer and dry powder. Each position sized so a full stop-hit costs ~1.3-1.5% of total equity, well within the 1-2% risk budget. Avoided TTD (SMA50 slope -9.9%, still falling knife), ADSK (SMA50 slope still declining, less compelling value than ADBE), and CDW (extended off SMA50 at +8.3%). Rejected PSKY (near-zero ROE, negative operating margin despite screening pass). Confidence in ~1% weekly compounding is moderate — these are quality setups but the macro backdrop remains uncertain and base formations can fail.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $50.00-$50.44 on any intraday pullback, or buy at market open if price holds above SMA50. Avoid chasing if extended more than 3% above current level.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: PayPal is the deepest value name in large-cap fintech — fwd P/E of 8.71, PEG 0.91, ROE 25.7%, $3.3B FCF, $6.4B operating cash flow. New CEO Alex Chriss executing a focused turnaround: cutting low-margin unbranded checkout, improving Braintree unit economics, and relaunching PayPal-branded checkout with personalization. The business generates substantial free cash with minimal capex. Trading near multi-year trough valuations that assume zero growth — any reacceleration is unpriced. TECHNICAL: Confirmed uptrend (basing), +8% above SMA50 with slope +2.3% — momentum turning positive. 30% of 52w range, well away from recent lows at $38.96. ATR 2.7% indicates controlled, non-panicky price action. This is a Stage 1/2 transition with the SMA50 already curling up.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) price closes below stop $47.72 on volume; (2) thesis breaks — revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters or management guides to materially lower FCF; (3) stock fails to make progress toward $60 within 90 days of entry (time stop); (4) target $70 hit, reassess. Consider holding to LTCG if stock is working and thesis intact at 11-month mark.

trades.entry_strategy: Buy at market or limit near $85-86. Prefer entry on any 1-2 day pullback toward the SMA50 (~$82). Do not chase if price runs more than 5% above current level before entry.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Fortinet is a best-in-class cybersecurity platform with exceptional economics — ROE 135.7%, operating margin 32.8%, FCF $1.7B. The convergence of network security and SASE/SD-WAN creates a multi-year upgrade cycle. Revenue growth 14.8% with expanding margins as hardware refresh cycle normalizes and services mix increases. Competitive moat in the SMB/mid-market segment is durable. TECHNICAL: Only candidate clearly above its SMA200 (+3.8%) — confirms genuine institutional accumulation, not just a relief bounce. Uptrend basing at 35% of 52w range. SMA50 slope +0.3% — momentum just turning. ATR 3.2% is orderly. This is the cleanest chart on the list — price held well through the April selloff relative to peers.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) price closes below $80.77; (2) revenue growth decelerates below 10% or billings growth turns negative; (3) no progress toward $95 within 60 days of entry (time stop); (4) target $108 reached near prior range highs — reassess for continuation or trim. Would consider holding to LTCG if cybersecurity spending remains robust and stock trends higher.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $242-245 only — do not buy at market. Wait for price to pull back to near 52w range support and show at least 1-2 days of stabilization. If price does not reach $245 within 2 weeks, re-evaluate; do not chase upward.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Adobe is arguably the highest-quality software franchise on this list — ROE 58.8%, operating margin 38.8%, FCF $9.3B, P/E 14.62 trailing / 9.50 forward. PEG 0.70 is exceptional. AI fear (generative image tools disrupting Creative Cloud) is massively overpriced into the stock — Adobe is integrating AI (Firefly) as an upsell, not a threat. Document Cloud and Experience Cloud are high-switching-cost recurring revenue. This is a $100B+ FCF business trading at less than 10x forward earnings. TECHNICAL: 13% of 52w range — near multi-year lows. The SMA50 slope (-5.4%) is the primary caution flag and is why we are using a limit entry below current price rather than buying now. Waiting for price to find support near $240-245 before committing. If SMA50 flattens over the next 2-4 weeks, this becomes higher conviction.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) price closes below $226 (2x ATR below limit entry); (2) Adobe reports meaningful Creative Cloud subscriber loss or revenue deceleration below 8% citing AI competition; (3) no evidence of SMA50 flattening within 45 days — revisit; (4) target $335 reached, trim 50% and let remainder run toward prior highs with trailing stop.
